key_insight: An expandable bank of modality-specific experts enables medical vision-language learning across imaging domains while preserving evaluated existing representations.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support reusable image classification and retrieval tools across medical imaging modalities, though clinical utility is not established.
method: Combine shared visual computation with deterministically routed modality experts and a separate text pathway.
Pretrain on unpaired images using modality-aware tokenization, then align images and text with contrastive learning.
Add fundus and OCT experts while freezing existing image and text embedding paths.
evidence_signal: Using 19.4 million unpaired image rows and 3.23 million image-text pairs, the model achieved best or tied-best results in 24 of 25 benchmark settings across nine modalities.
watch_item: Retention depends on unchanged existing computation paths and inference conditions; feature-identity checks verify preservation only on evaluated inputs.
paper_title: Expandable Modality Experts for Medical Vision-Language Learning
